learningObjectives: Explain application and production Rulesets in a scenario.
Explain Ruleset validation in a scenario.
Explain the Ruleset list in a scenario.

elements.description: Rulesets package related Rules. Application Rulesets define application behavior; organizational Rulesets support reuse. Int conventionally groups integration Rules. Production Rulesets support controlled maintenance in production, including delegation; keep a version unlocked and give intended operators access through their Access Groups.

elements.text: Worked example: Compliance staff maintain a delegated threshold in PolicyProd. Keep its editable version unlocked and configure the application plus the authorized Access Group.

elements.description: AV validates references against the defining application and its built-on stack. RV uses explicit version prerequisites and their prerequisites; prerequisite cycles are invalid. Validation happens at design time, not as runtime ranking. Use RV for portable shared assets. Revalidate after changes to built-on applications or the Ruleset list.

elements.text: Worked example: An RV integration module cannot reference a consumer-specific Rule merely because one developer can run that consumer. Its prerequisites must supply the dependency.

elements.description: At login, Pega starts from the Access Group’s versioned application and walks its built-on applications to assemble the runtime stack. Higher entries have precedence within Rule resolution. Eligible developers also get a personal Ruleset for checked-out Rules at the top. Inspect Operator Profile when two users see different behavior.

elements.text: Worked example: User One checks out a Rule; User Two does not. Compare their stack contexts before blaming the released Rule.

examPitfalls.title: Design vs execution
examPitfalls.trapDescription: RV decides which Rule wins at run time.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use validation for dependencies and the runtime stack for execution.

examPitfalls.title: Production access
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Application registration automatically grants access to everyone.

examPitfalls.title: Dependency direction
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A reusable lower application can reference any consuming application.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Keep references within the defining application and allowed dependencies.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Policy maintainers need controlled production edits. Which Ruleset category fits?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Production Rulesets support maintenance without redeploying the entire application.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Application and production Rulesets. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: A personal Ruleset isolates developer checkout work, not shared policy maintenance.
optionExplanations.B: Use a production Ruleset for authorized live policy changes.
optionExplanations.C: Platform Rulesets are not the container for this application-specific policy.
optionExplanations.D: Blocked is rule availability, not a Ruleset category.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A production Ruleset is declared on the application, but a manager cannot access it. Which configuration needs review?

options.text: The manager’s Access Group production Rulesets

practiceQuiz.rationale: Application declaration alone does not grant the operator access.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Application and production Rulesets. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Urgency prioritizes work; it does not grant Ruleset access.
optionExplanations.B: Circumstance dates specialize behavior, not operator access.
optionExplanations.C: Check the production Ruleset configuration of the manager’s Access Group.
optionExplanations.D: A skim target controls consolidation, not the manager’s access.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Two AV Rulesets in the same application reference each other. Is this inherently invalid?

options.text: Yes, all dependencies must be RV

practiceQuiz.rationale: AV supports codependent Rulesets in one application.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Ruleset validation. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: AV allows these references within the same application.
optionExplanations.B: RV is not mandatory for every application dependency.
optionExplanations.C: Skimming does not introduce permission for these references.
optionExplanations.D: Same-application codependency is valid in AV.

practiceQuiz.scenario: SharedCore uses RV and references CustomerData. What must be configured?
practiceQuiz.rationale: RV checks declared dependencies rather than unrestricted application access.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Ruleset validation. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Declare the needed CustomerData version as a prerequisite.
optionExplanations.B: A privilege cannot satisfy a development dependency.
optionExplanations.D: Checkout cannot supply the shared Ruleset dependency.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO statements about validation are correct?

options.text: It selects the runtime winning Rule
Application-stack changes can invalidate AV references
RV permits all Rules above the defining application

practiceQuiz.rationale: Validation checks dependencies; runtime selection is a different mechanism.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Ruleset validation. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Validation checks design dependencies, not runtime winners.
optionExplanations.B: A cyclic prerequisite chain is invalid in RV.
optionExplanations.C: Changing the stack can remove a previously valid AV target.
optionExplanations.D: RV references are restricted to declared prerequisite chains.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Two operators run different application versions. What determines the starting application for stack assembly?

options.text: The application on their Access Groups
The highest version anywhere in the database

practiceQuiz.rationale: Runtime context begins from the configured application.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on The Ruleset list. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Learning confidence has no runtime configuration role.
optionExplanations.B: The Access Group identifies the starting application version.
optionExplanations.C: A globally newer version is not automatically selected.
optionExplanations.D: Packaging inspection does not select the operator’s application.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer sees a checked-out edit while another operator sees released behavior. Which stack element explains this?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Checked-out Rules belong to the developer’s personal stack context.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on The Ruleset list. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: The developer’s personal Ruleset holds their checked-out edit.
optionExplanations.B: A work queue does not hold checked-out rules.
optionExplanations.C: An archive is a deployment artifact, not the developer’s runtime layer.
optionExplanations.D: A prerequisite cycle is an invalid dependency, not an isolated edit.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO requirements fit a delegated production Ruleset?

options.text: Copy it into every personal Ruleset

practiceQuiz.rationale: Maintainability and operator access are separate requirements.
practiceQuiz.hint: Focus on Application and production Rulesets. Identify the scope or context named in the question.

optionExplanations.A: Not Available would prevent normal selection of these rules.
optionExplanations.B: An unlocked version permits authorized production maintenance.
optionExplanations.C: Intended operators need the corresponding Access Group access.
optionExplanations.D: Personal copies do not provide shared delegated maintenance.

quickRecap.value: Editable version plus application declaration and intended Access Group access.
AV: defining application and built-on stack. RV: declared prerequisites; no cycles.
Access Group → application → built-on hierarchy; personal checkout sits above application Rules.
